args.subject: Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?
args.body:
Hi Tessa,

Thanks for reaching out. Here's a quote you can attribute to me:

"I started Halcyon Threshold because the conversation around superintelligence has been stuck in a false dichotomy — either we panic and stop everything, or we race ahead blindly. The labs are getting the timeline wrong (it's sooner than they say) and the architecture wrong (alignment isn't a patch you apply after the fact). We need to build the technical and governance infrastructure for a good outcome *now*, not hope someone else figures it out later."

Happy to do a quick call if you need more.

Best,
Morgan Hale
Founder, Halcyon Threshold

Halcyon Threshold

Building the infrastructure for a good superintelligence outcome

Home Mission Work Blog Contact

Our Mission

Superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happened to humanity — or the worst. The outcome depends on what we build *before* it arrives.

Halcyon Threshold exists to contribute to the best possible outcome. We work on the technical and governance infrastructure needed to steer superintelligence toward human flourishing: alignment research, safety evaluations, and policy groundwork.

We reject the false choice between panic and reckless acceleration. The path forward is deliberate, rigorous preparation — starting now.

Current Focus

  • → Scalable oversight — techniques for supervising systems smarter than their overseers
  • → Mechanistic interpretability — understanding what models actually compute
  • → Governance infrastructure — licensing, auditing, and compute thresholds for frontier runs

Get Involved

We're a small team looking for collaborators — researchers, engineers, policy analysts, and funders who share the mission. Reach out if you'd like to contribute.

Halcyon Threshold · morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

Founded by Morgan Hale

Mission

Why we exist and what we stand for

Home Mission Work Blog Contact

The Core Problem

Superintelligent AI — systems that exceed human capabilities across virtually all cognitive domains — is likely to be developed this decade. The consequences will be profound and irreversible. A good outcome is not guaranteed; it requires deliberate preparation.

Today, the field is polarized. One camp advocates pausing all progress out of fear. The other races ahead, treating safety as an afterthought. Both are mistakes. The first surrenders the immense benefits of superintelligence (curing disease, solving climate change, expanding human potential). The second gambles with existential risk.

Halcyon Threshold was founded to pursue a third path: rigorous, proactive preparation for a good outcome.

Our Principles

1. Timeline honesty

Superintelligence is closer than most institutions admit. Planning horizons of 10–20 years are dangerously complacent. We operate on the assumption that transformative systems arrive within 3–7 years.

2. Alignment is not a patch

You cannot build a dangerous system and "align it later." Alignment must be built into the architecture from the start. We fund and conduct research on scalable oversight, interpretability, and training objectives that make alignment the default.

3. Governance must keep pace

Technical solutions alone are insufficient. We need compute governance, licensing frameworks for frontier training runs, independent auditing, and international coordination — built before they're urgently needed.

4. Small team, high leverage

We don't need to do everything. We focus on the highest-leverage gaps: the work that unlocks other work, the research that shifts the field, the policy groundwork that enables coordination.

5. Epistemic humility

We don't have all the answers. We publish our reasoning, invite criticism, and update quickly. The goal is a good outcome, not being right.

What We Don't Do

  • We don't build frontier models ourselves — that race is well-funded.
  • We don't advocate for a permanent pause — the benefits of superintelligence are too large to forgo.
  • We don't treat "alignment" as a single problem with a single solution — it's a cluster of technical and governance challenges.
  • We don't work in secrecy — coordination requires transparency.

How We Measure Progress

We track concrete milestones: research papers published and cited; policy proposals adopted or cited in legislative processes; technical tools adopted by labs; funding moved toward high-impact alignment work; people recruited to the field.

Our north star: When superintelligence arrives, the probability of a good outcome is higher because Halcyon Threshold existed.

Halcyon Threshold · morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

Founded by Morgan Hale

What we're building, researching, and advocating for

Active Projects

A living synthesis of the current state of alignment research: scalable oversight (RLHF, RLAIF, debate, amplification), mechanistic interpretability (SAEs, causal tracing, activation patching), mechanistic anomaly detection, training objectives (CCTV, shard theory, corrigibility), and evaluation frameworks. Updated weekly.

Research Synthesis Open

Compute Governance Policy Memo

Drafting a concrete policy proposal for a tiered licensing regime for frontier training runs above 10^25 FLOP, with independent safety audits, compute reporting, and international coordination mechanisms. Target: submission to relevant congressional offices and UK AISI by Q1 2027.

Policy Governance

Research Priorities

  • Scalable oversight: How to supervise systems more capable than their overseers — debate, amplification, recursive reward modeling, and constitutional AI.
  • Mechanistic interpretability: Reverse-engineering learned algorithms in neural networks; sparse autoencoders, causal interventions, automated discovery.
  • Evaluation & red-teaming: Building benchmarks that actually measure dangerous capabilities (situational awareness, deception, autonomous replication).
  • Corrigibility & shutdown: Training objectives that preserve human control — not just "do what I mean" but "let me turn you off."
  • Multi-agent dynamics: Risks from interacting AI systems (collusion, steganography, emergent coordination).

Governance Priorities

  • Compute thresholds: Defining and enforcing compute-based licensing for frontier training runs.
  • Independent auditing: Building the auditor ecosystem, standards, and liability frameworks.
  • International coordination: Track-1.5 dialogues, shared compute accounting, verification regimes.
  • Liability & insurance: Clarifying developer liability for harms from frontier models.

Outputs (Coming Soon)

We publish our work openly. Expected outputs in the next quarter:

  • Alignment landscape review (living document, public)
  • Policy memo: "A Licensing Regime for Frontier AI Training Runs"
  • Technical report: "Evaluating Scalable Oversight Protocols on Frontier Models"
  • Blog series: "Why the Doom/Acceleration Binary Is Wrong"

fields.name: Morgan Hale
fields.comment:
Halcyon Threshold supports mandatory incident reporting for frontier AI models. However, the proposed 72-hour window is insufficient for complex incidents involving model autonomy, deception, or steganography. We recommend:

1. A tiered reporting timeline: 24 hours for confirmed capability demonstrations (autonomous replication, CBRN assistance, persuasive manipulation), 72 hours for other serious incidents.

2. A confidential pre-notification channel for incidents that could cause panic or be exploited if publicly disclosed immediately.

3. Mandatory third-party audit of incident response within 30 days, with results shared with the regulator.

4. A compute threshold trigger: all models trained above 10^25 FLOP are subject to this rule, regardless of developer size.

5. International harmonization: the rule should recognize equivalent reporting in allied jurisdictions to avoid regulatory arbitrage.

The current proposal is a good start but risks creating a checkbox compliance exercise. The goal must be genuine learning and adaptation, not just paperwork.

fields.project_title: Scalable Oversight Protocols for Frontier Model Evaluation
fields.summary:
We propose a 6-month research sprint to develop and evaluate scalable oversight protocols for frontier AI models. The core problem: as models exceed human capabilities, we lose the ability to supervise them directly. Current approaches (RLHF, constitutional AI, debate) have not been rigorously tested on frontier-class systems.

This project will: (1) build a modular evaluation framework for oversight protocols; (2) implement and test debate, amplification, and recursive reward modeling on frontier-accessible models (via API and open-weight); (3) develop metrics for oversight quality that correlate with downstream safety; (4) publish a technical report and open-source the evaluation infrastructure.

The work directly addresses the highest-leverage gap identified in our Alignment Techniques Landscape Review: we lack empirical evidence on which oversight protocols actually scale. This project produces that evidence and the tools for others to build on it.

Team: Morgan Hale (PI, alignment research), Priya Raman (data analyst, 5 hrs/week), seeking one additional research engineer. Budget: $22,500 (personnel $18k, compute credits $3k, travel/meetings $1.5k).
